title: [Direct-to-AIP] Asset Listing - USDC Plasma
author: @TokenLogic
created: 2026-11-18

Summary

This proposal seeks to onboard native USDC as a supported asset on the Aave V3 Plasma Instance.

Circle deployed USDC natively on Plasma on August 28, 2026, alongside EURC, the Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol, and Bridge Kit. This proposal expands the stablecoin offering on Aave V3 Plasma and gives users an additional highly liquid, fiat-backed asset for supplying, borrowing, and collateral use, configured in line with USDT0.

Motivation

On August 28, 2026, Circle announced native USDC on Plasma, along with institutional on and off ramps through Circle Mint. Circle issues native USDC on Plasma, fully reserved and redeemable 1:1 for US dollars through eligible Circle channels. CCTP enables native USDC to be transferred between Plasma and other supported networks without relying on wrapped or third-party bridged representations.

Aave V3 Plasma is today a USDT0-centric market. USDT0 is the only fiat-backed stablecoin listed and carries roughly $603M of supply against $552M of borrows (about 92% utilisation), with USDe and GHO as the other borrowable stablecoins. Every stablecoin-borrowing eMode category on the instance points to USDT0.

Onboarding USDC to Aave V3 Plasma would:

  • Add a second fiat-backed stablecoin to the instance, reducing single-issuer concentration on the stablecoin side of the book.
  • Provide an additional asset for lending and borrowing alongside USDT0, USDe, and GHO.
  • Increase the stablecoin borrowing liquidity available to the existing USDe, sUSDe, weETH, syrupUSDT, WXPL, GHO and PT-sUSDe eMode categories.
  • Enable users and institutions to access native USDC liquidity supported by Circle Mint and CCTP infrastructure, and to move USDC between Plasma and other Aave deployments (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Avalanche, X Layer) via CCTP.

Plasma is a stablecoin-focused network, and the arrival of Circle’s native issuance gives Aave V3 Plasma direct access to the second largest stablecoin without bridge dependencies.

Specification

USDC Contract Address

Asset Address
USDC 0x2d661C89D812261039AF9764eceaAee884f5F67F

The address above represents Circle-issued native USDC on Plasma (6 decimals), as published in Circle’s contract address reference.

Proposed Market Configuration

We propose configuring USDC in line with the parameters currently applied to USDT0 on Aave V3 Plasma, consistent with the approach LlamaRisk recommended for the recent USDC listing on X Layer (USDC aligned to the local USDT0 risk parameters, 75% LTV and 78% LT, with a CAPO stable adapter). Supply and borrow caps mirror the X Layer listing and can be raised through the Risk Steward as USDC liquidity on Plasma develops. Final parameters remain subject to Risk Service Provider recommendations.

Final onboarding parameters remain subject to review and recommendations from Aave’s Risk Service Providers.

Liquidity

Native USDC on Plasma is only days old: roughly 4.5M USDC has been minted at the time of writing, and on-chain DEX liquidity is still nascent. As with the X Layer listing, liquidity is expected to build as supply flows to the chain through CCTP and Circle Mint, and the proposed caps leave room for Risk Service Providers to sequence activation or adjust caps based on observed liquidity at execution.

eMode Configuration

We propose adding USDC as a borrowable asset to the eight current-generation eMode categories on Plasma in which USDT0 is borrowable today. This proposal does not modify the collateral, LTV, LT, or Liquidation Bonus parameters for any category; it only adds USDC as a borrowable asset to each mentioned eMode.

Oracle

A Chainlink USDC/USD Price Feed is already available on Plasma Mainnet.

Chainlink identifies this feed as USDC/USD-RefPrice-DF-Plasma-001.

We propose pricing USDC through the Chainlink USDC/USD feed wrapped in a CAPO stable adapter (PriceCapAdapterStable) with the upward price deviation capped at 4% ($1.04), in line with LlamaRisk’s recommendation for USDC on X Layer and identical to the cap of the Capped USDT/USD adapter (0xdBbB0b5DD13E7AC9C56624834ef193df87b022c3) currently used for USDT0 on Plasma. The final oracle configuration is to be confirmed by the relevant Aave Risk and Technical Service Providers.

Disclaimer

TokenLogic is an active service provider to the Aave DAO, the beneficiary of stream 100086 and the KPI as outlined in this publication. The scope of this engagement is available via this forum proposal.

TokenLogic supports and maintains an independent delegate voting platform within the Aave community.

TokenLogic and associated entities have no undisclosed material conflicts of interest at the time of submission.

Next Steps

  1. Gather feedback from the community.
  2. Using the Direct-to-AIP process, incorporate feedback from the Risk Service Provider.
  3. Escalate this proposal to the AIP Voting stage.

governance_posts.title: [ARFC] Expand Coinbase Tokenized Equities on Base
governance_posts.description:
Summary

This ARFC proposes to expand the Aave V4 Equities Hub on Base with six Coinbase tokenized equities as collateral: Netflix (NFLXc), Oracle (ORCLc), Palantir Technologies (PLTRc), Advanced Micro Devices (AMDc), ServiceNow (NOWc), and Strategy (MSTRc). The first five are S&P 500 constituents and Strategy is listed on Nasdaq outside the index. All six are issued on the same Base stack as the Magnificent Seven (Mag7) tokens already on the hub, namely the B20 token standard and Coinbase’s Token Supply Manager, and are to be priced by Chainlink total return feeds on the 24/5 template of the existing reserves. MSTRc’s feed is already live. They would join the Mag-7 Spoke as collateral only, with USDC as the borrowable asset, under the same market structure as the existing reserves.

Reserve Volatility, 1 year Collateral Factor Max Liquidation Bonus Add Cap
NFLXc 36.2% 65% 5.50% 79,038 (USD 5.00M)
ORCLc 59.2% 58% 5.50% 42,378 (USD 5.00M)
PLTRc 58.9% 58% 5.50% 29,617 (USD 5.00M)
AMDc 72.9% 49% 5.50% 9,704 (USD 5.00M)
NOWc 66.7% 50% 5.50% 50,195 (USD 5.00M)
MSTRc 81.1% 47% 6.50% 41,298 (USD 5.00M)

Source: LlamaRisk, November 12, 2026

The six stocks trade between USD 1.8B and 10.9B a day in their cash markets, and all six have perpetual markets on Binance, Hyperliquid, and OKX. The more volatile a stock, the lower its collateral factor, which is capped at 65%. NFLX moves about as much as the Mag7 stocks already on the hub, whose volatility ranges from 25.0% to 46.3%, while ORCL, PLTR, AMD, NOW and MSTR move more than any of them. The maximum liquidation bonus is 5.5% on the first five, the same as the Mag7 reserves on the spoke, and 6.5% on MSTRc, which also carries a 10% risk premium. The add caps are set at USD 5M of collateral per token, USD 30.0M in total, and the spoke’s unchanged USDC draw cap of USD 21M bounds what the hub’s USDC suppliers lend against the equities on the spoke.

Motivation

The Equities Hub currently holds eight tokenized equities alongside USDC. Onboarding the six tokens would:

  • Broaden the collateral on the hub with large-cap US equities whose cash markets trade between USD 1.8B and 10.9B a day.
  • Add collateral issued under the same program, token standard, and price feed design as the existing reserves, so that the market structure, liquidation routes, and oracle setup of the hub apply without change.
  • Allow borrowers on the pooled spoke to hold more diversified collateral positions, with each asset keeping its own collateral factor.

1. The Six Stocks

Five of the six are S&P 500 constituents. Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, is listed on Nasdaq and is not a member of the index. All six have trading histories back to 2018 or earlier, except Palantir, which listed in September 2020. Each clears the listing floor of USD 2B of market capitalization and USD 50M of median daily traded value by a factor of 25 or more, and none of the six reports substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern in its latest annual or quarterly report.

Token Company Listing Market cap Daily traded value, 63-session median Dividend Quarterly results
NFLXc Netflix Nasdaq USD 259.8B USD 2.4B None Reported 2026-10-20, next expected January 2027
ORCLc Oracle NYSE USD 366.9B USD 3.8B Quarterly, USD 0.50 Reported 2026-09-10, next expected December 2026
PLTRc Palantir Technologies Nasdaq USD 406.8B USD 4.4B None Reported 2026-11-02, next expected February 2027
AMDc Advanced Micro Devices Nasdaq USD 845.0B USD 10.9B None Reported 2026-11-03, next expected February 2027
NOWc ServiceNow NYSE USD 103.4B USD 1.8B None Reported 2026-10-28, next expected January 2027
MSTRc Strategy Nasdaq USD 51.1B USD 2.7B None Reported 2026-10-29, next expected February 2027

Source: SEC EDGAR and Yahoo Finance, November 10, 2026

Market capitalization counts every share class at the close of November 10, 2026. Daily traded value is the median daily dollar volume over the 63 sessions to the same date.

Oracle is the only one of the six that pays a dividend on its common stock. Strategy pays dividends on its preferred stock only. Dividends and other corporate actions reach the tokens through the issuer multiplier, as described in Section 4 of the technical review. The ORCLc multiplier stands at 1.00004, set on October 23, 2026, the pay date of Oracle’s last dividend. Oracle’s next dividend has not been declared. None of the six companies has announced a split, a spin-off, a tender offer, a delisting, or a merger in which it is the target.

Strategy held 848,517 bitcoin on October 25, 2026, worth USD 68.3B, more than its market capitalization. Its convertible notes (USD 6.7B) and preferred stock (about USD 14.1B of liquidation preference) rank ahead of the Class A shares the token tracks, according to its quarterly report for the quarter to September 30, 2026.

2. Price Behavior

Volatility is the annualized standard deviation of daily close-to-close log returns. The drawdown is the largest peak-to-trough fall of the closing price. Earnings nights are the nights with a quarterly results filing among each stock’s ten largest falls from a close to the next open since 2019.

Stock Volatility, 1 year Volatility, 30 sessions Worst day since 2018 Largest drawdown, 1 year Earnings nights among the 10 worst
NFLX 36.2% 34.5% -35.1% -46.4% 8
ORCL 59.2% 70.1% -13.8% -53.7% 6
PLTR 58.9% 55.8% -21.3% -44.8% 6
AMD 72.9% 97.1% -17.3% -37.7% 3
NOW 66.7% 100.7% -27.0% -52.2% 4
MSTR 81.1% 71.6% -25.5% -65.5% 0
Mag7 range 25.0% to 46.3% 23.0% to 52.2% -12.6% to -26.4% -13.8% to -39.1% 2 to 7

Source: Yahoo Finance and SEC EDGAR, November 10, 2026

ORCL, PLTR, AMD, NOW and MSTR moved with annualized volatility of 58.9% to 81.1% over the past year, above TSLA at 46.3%, the most volatile of the Mag7. MSTR is the most volatile of the six. NFLX, at 36.2%, sits within the Mag7 range. Over the last 30 sessions AMD and NOW rose to 97.1% and 100.7%, after their quarterly results on November 3 and October 28, 2026.

NOW’s worst day since 2018 was its results session of October 29, 2026, a fall of 27.0%. Earnings nights account for three to eight of the ten largest falls from a close to the next open for each of the first five, so their largest overnight moves cluster around scheduled quarterly releases. Six of MSTR’s ten largest falls came over weekends, when bitcoin trades and the stock does not, and none on a results night. ORCL, NOW and MSTR also fell 53.7%, 52.2% and 65.5% from peak to trough over the past year.


Source: Yahoo Finance, November 10, 2026

Each of the six feeds is expected to meet these requirements, as MSTRc’s live feed does:

  • It prices the token as the underlying share price times the issuer multiplier, as on the listed reserves.
  • It publishes through the pre-market, regular, post-market and overnight sessions, from Sunday 20:00 to Friday 20:00 ET.
  • It updates on a deviation threshold of at most 0.5%, the oracle allowance in the collateral factor, and a heartbeat of at most 24 hours within those sessions.

The feeds stop updating from Friday 20:00 to Sunday 20:00 ET and on US market holidays, and keep showing the last price. Positions can still be liquidated in that window, but only at that price, so a move in the stock over the weekend reaches positions when the feed restarts on Sunday evening.

3. Perpetual Futures

Perpetual futures let a liquidator hedge seized collateral while the cash market is closed. All six names trade on Binance, Hyperliquid, and OKX, and all except NFLX on Lighter. Open interest is counted once per contract on every venue, so Hyperliquid’s reported figure, which sums long and short positions, is halved.

On November 11, 2026 open interest across the four venues ranged from USD 3.05M (NOW) to USD 42.07M (AMD) on the first five, and 24-hour volume from USD 2.64M (NOW) to USD 441.07M (AMD). MSTR carried USD 111.17M of open interest and USD 362.25M of 24-hour volume on November 12, 2026, more open interest than any Mag7 name except GOOGL and NVDA. Only AMD and MSTR exceed the smallest Mag7 total, USD 33.52M on AMZN, while the largest, NVDA, carries USD 543.06M. Binance holds the largest share of open interest on all six names. Turnover relative to open interest is highest on AMD, at about 10.5 times its open interest in a day.

Perpetual markets on MSTR, AMD and ORCL are deep enough to hedge a large liquidation. A quarter of a full USD 5M cap is about 1.1% of MSTR’s open interest. On PLTR, NFLX and NOW they are thinner, so a hedge of a quarter of a full cap, USD 1.25M, would move their price, especially at weekends. The hedge is not needed to protect the market: the collateral factor covers the fall until the next regular session, when seized tokens can be redeemed or sold, and the cap limits the amount at risk to USD 5M per token.


Source: Binance, Hyperliquid, OKX and Lighter, November 11, 2026

Over the last 30 days, median weekday volume across the four venues ranged from USD 3.3M (NOW) to USD 345.9M (MSTR), with weekend volume at a ninth to about a fifth of weekday levels. Open interest on Binance and OKX roughly halved on PLTR (USD 16.7M to 8.9M), eased on ORCL (USD 25.7M to 17.6M), held steady on NFLX (USD 7.0M to 6.9M), and ended level on AMD (USD 29.1M to 28.3M) after a peak of USD 56.2M around its results. On NOW it rose from USD 1.6M to 1.9M, after a peak of about USD 5.5M in the session after its results, and on MSTR from USD 92.7M to 99.0M.


*Source: Binance, Hyperliquid, **OKX *and Lighter, October 12 to November 10, 2026


Source: Binance and OKX, October 12 to November 10, 2026

4. The Tokens on Base

Each token is a CB Certificate issued by Coinbase Onchain SPV Ltd under a series prospectus approved by the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Abu Dhabi Global Market between September 3 and October 7, 2026 (NFLXc, ORCLc, PLTRc, AMDc, NOWc, MSTRc). Apart from the series details, the description of the underlying issuer, and minor drafting changes, the NFLXc, ORCLc, PLTRc, AMDc and NOWc prospectuses carry the text of the SpaceX prospectus of September 3, 2026, whose terms and conditions and deed of trust are those of the NVIDIA series examined in the technical review and the SPCXc assessment. The MSTRc prospectus, approved the same day as SpaceX’s, differs from it in the series details only. The tokens use the same B20 standard and Token Supply Manager as the listed reserves, and their admin, operator, pause, metadata, mint, and burn roles are held by the same addresses as on the listed Coinbase tokens.

Anyone who acquires the tokens on the secondary market, a liquidator included, holds them as an unvested holder, with no redemption right until it completes the issuer’s vesting process. The issuer’s operator can change a token’s multiplier by any amount in one transaction, and the feed carries the new value into the price at its next update. Announced corporate actions run with the issuer’s registry pause, during which the feed holds its last value and minting and redemption stop. The six reserves take this price setup on the same terms as the listed Coinbase reserves.

Token Series prospectus First mint Supply Mints / redemptions Mint allowance per 24h DEX depth at 2% impact Multiplier
NFLXc 2026-09-24 2026-09-24 7,953.59 (USD 503k) 104 / 41 70,100 (USD 4.43M) USD 203k 1.00000
ORCLc 2026-09-25 2026-09-28 3,073.19 (USD 363k) 87 / 36 35,800 (USD 4.22M) USD 129k 1.00004
PLTRc 2026-09-24 2026-09-24 2,879.10 (USD 486k) 213 / 204 26,100 (USD 4.41M) USD 148k 1.00000
AMDc 2026-09-25 2026-09-28 1,059.92 (USD 546k) 105 / 44 7,900 (USD 4.07M) USD 212k 1.00000
NOWc 2026-10-07 Not minted 0 0 / 0 36,200 (USD 3.61M) None 1.00000
MSTRc 2026-09-03 2026-09-03 19,506.98 (USD 2.36M) 731 / 517 40,800 (USD 4.94M) USD 230k 1.00000

Source: Basescan and KyberSwap, November 11, 2026

The daily mint allowance of each token is sized to USD 3.6M to 4.4M of notional per 24 hours on the first five and USD 4.9M on MSTRc, against USD 4.1M to 5.5M for the Mag7 tokens. The tokens carry no supply cap, and the minter’s 24-hour allowance is the only limit on new supply, which the issuance administrator can raise in one transaction. The add caps bound the hub’s exposure to each token whatever its supply. Supply stands between USD 363k and 546k per minted token of the first five, and NOWc has not yet been minted. MSTRc’s supply of USD 2.36M lies within the Mag7 range of USD 1.40M to 10.27M, and it carries the most primary activity, with 731 mints and 517 redemptions since September 3, 2026.

Secondary liquidity on Base for the first five is thinner than on the listed tokens. Between USD 129k and 212k of each minted token sells into USDC within a 2% price impact, against USD 246k (TSLAc) to 569k (AMZNc) for the Mag7 tokens. Each of the four minted tokens among them sells through a single Aerodrome Slipstream pool, whose liquidity range runs out before the price moves 2%. NOWc has no pool with usable depth. MSTRc sells USD 230k within 2%, inside the Mag7 range, across several Aerodrome pools and request-for-quote market makers.

5. Parameters

The six reserves join the pooled lending spoke of the Equities Hub on the same terms as the existing collateral: collateral only, a 10% liquidation fee, receive-shares enabled, and a collateral risk of 0, or 10% on MSTRc.

5.1 Collateral Factor

In Aave V4 the collateral factor is both the borrowing limit and the liquidation threshold. For a stock priced 24/5, it has to cover the largest fall from any off-hours price to the lowest price before five minutes past the next regular open, plus a 0.5% allowance for the feed’s deviation threshold. It is sized so that this fall exceeds a stock’s haircut on one night per stock in ten years, with a 2020-type crash counted as one year in ten.

The haircut scales a forecast of the stock’s daily volatility over the next year by the size of a once-in-ten-years off-hours fall relative to daily volatility, measured across S&P 500 stocks. The forecast weights the stock’s recent moves and pulls them partly toward the market-wide level. The collateral factor is what remains after the haircut, the maximum liquidation bonus and an allowance for interest while a position waits for liquidation, rounded down to a whole point and capped at 65%, which binds on NFLXc. At a 5.5% maximum liquidation bonus, the cap is a minimum haircut of 31.25%.

Reserve Daily returns Recent volatility, annualized Haircut Collateral factor
NFLXc 6,155 35.8% 24.49% 65%
ORCLc 10,244 63.0% 38.31% 58%
PLTRc 1,534 61.7% 37.70% 58%
AMDc 11,757 82.9% 47.67% 49%
NOWc 3,610 79.6% 46.15% 50%
MSTRc 7,147 80.8% 49.28% 47%

Source: Yahoo Finance, November 10, 2026

NFLXc carries the highest collateral factor of the six, with recent volatility of 35.8% a year. AMDc and NOWc sit at the low end, as their results nights of November 3-4 and October 28-29, 2026 took their recent volatility to 82.9% and 79.6% a year. MSTRc carries the lowest, 47%, although its recent volatility of 80.8% sits between theirs. Strategy is not an S&P 500 member, so its haircut uses the larger scale the method sets for stocks outside the index.

The collateral factors are set in full at listing and then reviewed with every listed stock at the last session of December, with a lower factor phased in over 10 sessions. The interest allowance charges 24% a year over the longest market closure, 92 hours and 35 minutes. That is the top of the hub’s USDC rate curve, so it covers the full curve.

*Source: **Aave *and Yahoo Finance, November 11, 2026

5.2 Liquidation Bonus

The maximum liquidation bonus is 5.5% on the first five, the value of the Mag7 reserves on the spoke, kept until the market has a longer liquidation history. MSTRc carries 6.5%, one point more, as SPCXc does, since its weekend gaps reach positions all at once when the feed reopens. Liquidators are relied on to liquidate positions and rotate the seized tokens within about 30 minutes in the US regular session. The spoke’s bonus curve pays 90% of the maximum at a health factor of 1.0 and the full maximum from a health factor of 0.90, so the first five pay 4.95% at a health factor of 1.0 and 5.5% from 0.90, and MSTRc 5.85% and 6.5%. At a health factor just below 1.0 the liquidator keeps about 4.46% of the repaid debt after the protocol’s 10% share, 5.27% on MSTRc, against the 2.6% a hedge costs in the regular session.

A liquidator with redemption access, a vested holder or an authorised participant, can redeem seized tokens through the issuer during regular hours. A liquidator without it sells on Base or hedges with a perpetual short until it can sell. With secondary depth of USD 129k to 230k at a 2% price impact, liquidations beyond small sizes go through redemption or a perpetual hedge.

5.3 Caps

The caps limit the size a liquidator may have to absorb. Each add cap starts at USD 5M of collateral, rises with the supply on the reserve to keep room for new deposits, and never exceeds the stock’s median daily traded value over the last 63 sessions, USD 1.8B to 10.9B for these six. The token counts below are at the close of November 10, 2026. The caps are reviewed daily after listing.

Reserve Hard cap, 63-session median daily traded value DEX depth at 2% impact Token supply Add cap Add cap, USD
NFLXc USD 2.43B USD 203k 7,953.59 (USD 503k) 79,038 USD 5.00M
ORCLc USD 3.82B USD 129k 3,073.19 (USD 363k) 42,378 USD 5.00M
PLTRc USD 4.37B USD 148k 2,879.10 (USD 486k) 29,617 USD 5.00M
AMDc USD 10.87B USD 212k 1,059.92 (USD 546k) 9,704 USD 5.00M
NOWc USD 1.82B None 0 50,195 USD 5.00M
MSTRc USD 2.74B USD 230k 19,506.98 (USD 2.36M) 41,298 USD 5.00M

Source: Yahoo Finance, Basescan and KyberSwap, November 11, 2026

At a hard cap of one day’s trading, a quarter of a capped supply liquidated at once and sold at a quarter of the market’s pace fits in one regular session. For these six, a quarter of USD 5M is USD 1.25M, against USD 1.8B to 10.9B traded each day on US venues.

Together the caps amount to USD 30.0M of collateral, which supports USD 16.3M of USDC debt at the proposed collateral factors. The caps on NFLXc, ORCLc, PLTRc and AMDc are 9 to 14 times each token’s supply on November 11, 2026, NOWc has no supply, and MSTRc’s cap is 2.1 times its supply. The issuer mints tokens on demand, and supply may follow the collateral demand of the market. USDC debt on the spoke stood at USD 7.01M on November 11, 2026, against the 21M USDC draw cap, and the USDC caps on the spoke are unchanged.

5.4 Risk Premium

MSTRc carries a collateral risk of 10%, while the other five stay at 0, as do the Mag7. The premium raises the borrow rate only on the part of a borrower’s debt that relies on MSTRc.

Specification

Market Composition

The six reserves join the Mag-7 Spoke, which holds the seven Magnificent Seven tokens and SPCXc as collateral, with USDC as the only borrowable asset. Summary

This ARFC proposes to expand the Aave V4 Equities Hub on Base with six Coinbase tokenized equities as collateral: Netflix (NFLXc), Oracle (ORCLc), Palantir Technologies (PLTRc), Advanced Micro Devices (AMDc), ServiceNow (NOWc), and Strategy (MSTRc). The first five are S&P 500 constituents and Strategy is listed on Nasdaq outside the index. All six are issued on the same Base stack as the Magnificent Seven (Mag7) tokens already on the hub, namely the B20 token standard and Coinbase’s Token Supply Manager, and are to be priced by Chainlink total return feeds on the 24/5 template of the existing reserves. MSTRc’s feed is already live. They would join the Mag-7 Spoke as collateral only, with USDC as the borrowable asset, under the same market structure as the existing reserves.

NOWc 66.7% 50% 5.50% 50,195 (USD 5.00M)
MSTRc 81.1% 47% 6.50% 41,298 (USD 5.00M)

Source: LlamaRisk, November 12, 2026

The six stocks trade between USD 1.8B and 10.9B a day in their cash markets, and all six have perpetual markets on Binance, Hyperliquid, and OKX. The more volatile a stock, the lower its collateral factor, which is capped at 65%. NFLX moves about as much as the Mag7 stocks already on the hub, whose volatility ranges from 25.0% to 46.3%, while ORCL, PLTR, AMD, NOW and MSTR move more than any of them. The maximum liquidation bonus is 5.5% on the first five, the same as the Mag7 reserves on the spoke, and 6.5% on MSTRc, which also carries a 10% risk premium. The add caps are set at USD 5M of collateral per token, USD 30.0M in total, and the spoke’s unchanged USDC draw cap of USD 21M bounds what the hub’s USDC suppliers lend against the equities on the spoke.

Motivation

The Equities Hub currently holds eight tokenized equities alongside USDC. Onboarding the six tokens would:

  • Broaden the collateral on the hub with large-cap US equities whose cash markets trade between USD 1.8B and 10.9B a day.
  • Add collateral issued under the same program, token standard, and price feed design as the existing reserves, so that the market structure, liquidation routes, and oracle setup of the hub apply without change.
  • Allow borrowers on the pooled spoke to hold more diversified collateral positions, with each asset keeping its own collateral factor.

1. The Six Stocks

Five of the six are S&P 500 constituents. Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, is listed on Nasdaq and is not a member of the index. All six have trading histories back to 2018 or earlier, except Palantir, which listed in September 2020. Each clears the listing floor of USD 2B of market capitalization and USD 50M of median daily traded value by a factor of 25 or more, and none of the six reports substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern in its latest annual or quarterly report.

Oracle is the only one of the six that pays a dividend on its common stock. Strategy pays dividends on its preferred stock only. Dividends and other corporate actions reach the tokens through the issuer multiplier, as described in Section 4 of the technical review. The ORCLc multiplier stands at 1.00004, set on October 23, 2026, the pay date of Oracle’s last dividend. Oracle’s next dividend has not been declared. Strategy held 848,517 bitcoin on October 25, 2026, worth USD 68.3B, more than its market capitalization. Its convertible notes (USD 6.7B) and preferred stock (about USD 14.1B of liquidation preference) rank ahead of the Class A shares the token tracks, according to its quarterly report for the quarter to September 30, 2026.

2. Price Behavior

Volatility is the annualized standard deviation of daily close-to-close log returns. The drawdown is the largest peak-to-trough fall of the closing price. Earnings nights are the nights with a quarterly results filing among each stock’s ten largest falls from a close to the next open since 2019.

ORCL, PLTR, AMD, NOW and MSTR moved with annualized volatility of 58.9% to 81.1% over the past year, above TSLA at 46.3%, the most volatile of the Mag7. MSTR is the most volatile of the six. NFLX, at 36.2%, sits within the Mag7 range. Over the last 30 sessions AMD and NOW rose to 97.1% and 100.7%, after their quarterly results on November 3 and October 28, 2026.

NOW’s worst day since 2018 was its results session of October 29, 2026, a fall of 27.0%. Earnings nights account for three to eight of the ten largest falls from a close to the next open for each of the first five, so their largest overnight moves cluster around scheduled quarterly releases. Six of MSTR’s ten largest falls came over weekends, when bitcoin trades and the stock does not, and none on a results night. ORCL, NOW and MSTR also fell 53.7%, 52.2% and 65.5% from peak to trough over the past year.


Source: Yahoo Finance, November 10, 2026

Each of the six feeds is expected to meet these requirements, as MSTRc’s live feed does:

  • It prices the token as the underlying share price times the issuer multiplier, as on the listed reserves.
  • It publishes through the pre-market, regular, post-market and overnight sessions, from Sunday 20:00 to Friday 20:00 ET.
  • It updates on a deviation threshold of at most 0.5%, the oracle allowance in the collateral factor, and a heartbeat of at most 24 hours within those sessions.

The feeds stop updating from Friday 20:00 to Sunday 20:00 ET and on US market holidays, and keep showing the last price. Positions can still be liquidated in that window, but only at that price, so a move in the stock over the weekend reaches positions when the feed restarts on Sunday evening.

3. Perpetual Futures

Perpetual futures let a liquidator hedge seized collateral while the cash market is closed. All six names trade on Binance, Hyperliquid, and OKX, and all except NFLX on Lighter. Open interest is counted once per contract on every venue, so Hyperliquid’s reported figure, which sums long and short positions, is halved.

On November 11, 2026 open interest across the four venues ranged from USD 3.05M (NOW) to USD 42.07M (AMD) on the first five, and 24-hour volume from USD 2.64M (NOW) to USD 441.07M (AMD). MSTR carried USD 111.17M of open interest and USD 362.25M of 24-hour volume on November 12, 2026, more open interest than any Mag7 name except GOOGL and NVDA. Only AMD and MSTR exceed the smallest Mag7 total, USD 33.52M on AMZN, while the largest, NVDA, carries USD 543.06M. Binance holds the largest share of open interest on all six names. Turnover relative to open interest is highest on AMD, at about 10.5 times its open interest in a day.

Perpetual markets on MSTR, AMD and ORCL are deep enough to hedge a large liquidation. A quarter of a full USD 5M cap is about 1.1% of MSTR’s open interest. On PLTR, NFLX and NOW they are thinner, so a hedge of a quarter of a full cap, USD 1.25M, would move their price, especially at weekends. The hedge is not needed to protect the market: the collateral factor covers the fall until the next regular session, when seized tokens can be redeemed or sold, and the cap limits the amount at risk to USD 5M per token.


Source: Binance, Hyperliquid, OKX and Lighter, November 11, 2026

Over the last 30 days, median weekday volume across the four venues ranged from USD 3.3M (NOW) to USD 345.9M (MSTR), with weekend volume at a ninth to about a fifth of weekday levels. Open interest on Binance and OKX roughly halved on PLTR (USD 16.7M to 8.9M), eased on ORCL (USD 25.7M to 17.6M), held steady on NFLX (USD 7.0M to 6.9M), and ended level on AMD (USD 29.1M to 28.3M) after a peak of USD 56.2M around its results. On NOW it rose from USD 1.6M to 1.9M, after a peak of about USD 5.5M in the session after its results, and on MSTR from USD 92.7M to 99.0M.


*Source: Binance, Hyperliquid, **OKX *and Lighter, October 12 to November 10, 2026


Source: Binance and OKX, October 12 to November 10, 2026

4. The Tokens on Base

Each token is a CB Certificate issued by Coinbase Onchain SPV Ltd under a series prospectus approved by the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Abu Dhabi Global Market between September 3 and October 7, 2026 (NFLXc, ORCLc, PLTRc, AMDc, NOWc, MSTRc). Apart from the series details, the description of the underlying issuer, and minor drafting changes, the NFLXc, ORCLc, PLTRc, AMDc and NOWc prospectuses carry the text of the SpaceX prospectus of September 3, 2026, whose terms and conditions and deed of trust are those of the NVIDIA series examined in the technical review and the SPCXc assessment. The MSTRc prospectus, approved the same day as SpaceX’s, differs from it in the series details only. The tokens use the same B20 standard and Token Supply Manager as the listed reserves, and their admin, operator, pause, metadata, mint, and burn roles are held by the same addresses as on the listed Coinbase tokens.

Anyone who acquires the tokens on the secondary market, a liquidator included, holds them as an unvested holder, with no redemption right until it completes the issuer’s vesting process. The issuer’s operator can change a token’s multiplier by any amount in one transaction, and the feed carries the new value into the price at its next update. Announced corporate actions run with the issuer’s registry pause, during which the feed holds its last value and minting and redemption stop. The six reserves take this price setup on the same terms as the listed Coinbase reserves.

5. Parameters

The six reserves join the pooled lending spoke of the Equities Hub on the same terms as the existing collateral: collateral only, a 10% liquidation fee, receive-shares enabled, and a collateral risk of 0, or 10% on MSTRc.

5.1 Collateral Factor

In Aave V4 the collateral factor is both the borrowing limit and the liquidation threshold. For a stock priced 24/5, it has to cover the largest fall from any off-hours price to the lowest price before five minutes past the next regular open, plus a 0.5% allowance for the feed’s deviation threshold. It is sized so that this fall exceeds a stock’s haircut on one night per stock in ten years, with a 2020-type crash counted as one year in ten.

The haircut scales a forecast of the stock’s daily volatility over the next year by the size of a once-in-ten-years off-hours fall relative to daily volatility, measured across S&P 500 stocks. The forecast weights the stock’s recent moves and pulls them partly toward the market-wide level. The collateral factor is what remains after the haircut, the maximum liquidation bonus and an allowance for interest while a position waits for liquidation, rounded down to a whole point and capped at 65%, which binds on NFLXc. At a 5.5% maximum liquidation bonus, the cap is a minimum haircut of 31.25%.

5.2 Liquidation Bonus

The maximum liquidation bonus is 5.5% on the first five, the value of the Mag7 reserves on the spoke, kept until the market has a longer liquidation history. MSTRc carries 6.5%, one point more, as SPCXc does, since its weekend gaps reach positions all at once when the feed reopens. Liquidators are relied on to liquidate positions and rotate the seized tokens within about 30 minutes in the US regular session. The spoke’s bonus curve pays 90% of the maximum at a health factor of 1.0 and the full maximum from a health factor of 0.90, so the first five pay 4.95% at a health factor of 1.0 and 5.5% from 0.90, and MSTRc 5.85% and 6.5%. At a health factor just below 1.0 the liquidator keeps about 4.46% of the repaid debt after the protocol’s 10% share, 5.27% on MSTRc, against the 2.6% a hedge costs in the regular session.

A liquidator with redemption access, a vested holder or an authorised participant, can redeem seized tokens through the issuer during regular hours. A liquidator without it sells on Base or hedges with a perpetual short until it can sell. 5.3 Caps

The caps limit the size a liquidator may have to absorb. governance_posts.description:
Hi dear aave community :)

I’d like to share Aave DeFi Watcher, a browser extension I built to make monitoring Aave positions simple, fast, and privacy-friendly.

I originally started building it because the previously shared Aave Monitor extension appears to no longer function reliably. For example, many addresses currently return “Failed to fetch” instead of account data. It also only supports Aave V3, while I wanted a tool that could monitor positions across Aave V2, V3, and V4. Since I needed a working solution myself, I decided to build one from scratch.

Features

  • Total Collateral
  • Total Debt
  • Available to Borrow
  • Loan-to-Value (LTV)
  • Liquidation Threshold
  • Health Factor
  • Monitor multiple wallet addresses
  • Support for Aave V2, V3, and V4
  • Support for multiple networks including Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon, and Avalanche
  • Desktop notifications for Health Factor alerts
  • Privacy Mode to hide balances while continuing to monitor your positions
  • Automatic RPC fallback for improved reliability

One of my favorite features is the extension badge, which displays the Health Factor of your selected address directly on the browser toolbar, allowing you to monitor your position at a glance.

The extension is completely read-only. It never asks you to connect a wallet or sign transactions. All account data is fetched directly from Aave’s public smart contracts.

Monitor your Aave health factor and liquidation risk in real time across chains.

I built this extension for my own daily use and decided to share it with the community. It’s actively maintained, and I plan to continue adding new features and supporting future Aave releases.

I’d really appreciate any feedback, bug reports or feature suggestions from the community :))

I’d like to share Aave DeFi Watcher, a browser extension I built to make monitoring Aave positions simple, fast, and privacy-friendly.

I originally started building it because the previously shared Aave Monitor extension appears to no longer function reliably. For example, many addresses currently return “Failed to fetch” instead of account data. It also only supports Aave V3, while I wanted a tool that could monitor positions across Aave V2, V3, and V4. Since I needed a working solution myself, I decided to build one from scratch.

Features

  • Total Collateral
  • Total Debt
  • Available to Borrow
  • Loan-to-Value (LTV)
  • Liquidation Threshold
  • Health Factor
  • Monitor multiple wallet addresses
  • Support for Aave V2, V3, and V4
  • Support for multiple networks including Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon, and Avalanche
  • Desktop notifications for Health Factor alerts
  • Privacy Mode to hide balances while continuing to monitor your positions
  • Automatic RPC fallback for improved reliability

One of my favorite features is the extension badge, which displays the Health Factor of your selected address directly on the browser toolbar, allowing you to monitor your position at a glance.

The extension is completely read-only. It never asks you to connect a wallet or sign transactions. All account data is fetched directly from Aave’s public smart contracts.

Chrome Web Store

chromewebstore.google.com

Aave DeFi Watcher - Chrome Web Store

Monitor your Aave health factor and liquidation risk in real time across chains.

I built this extension for my own daily use and decided to share it with the community. It’s actively maintained, and I plan to continue adding new features and supporting future Aave releases.

I’d really appreciate any feedback, bug reports or feature suggestions from the community :))

title: [Research] Targeted Deleveraging of rsETH and osETH Through Exchange Rate Growth Discounting

author: @TokenLogic

created: 2026-11-24

Summary

LlamaRisk’s ARFC: Repositioning Aave V3 Core Around Established & Liquid Collateral proposes a WETH borrow rate increase as the final follow up control for the rsETH and osETH loops, should voluntary migration and natural unwinding prove insufficient.

This analysis proposes a more targeted alternative before resorting to a WETH borrow rate increase: setting maxYearlyRatioGrowthPercent to 0% on the rsETH and osETH CAPO adapters. Unlike a WETH borrow rate increase, this approach does not impose additional borrowing costs across the entire WETH reserve.

For rsETH, the unwinding timeline can be accelerated further through sized E-Mode liquidation threshold reductions, following an initial borrower engagement and migration window. This provides a more targeted path to reducing exposure while preserving the migration route proposed in LlamaRisk’s ARFC.

Motivation

A WETH borrow rate increase applies to the entire WETH reserve, affecting every ETH loop on Core, including wstETH and weETH positions that the ARFC intends to retain. This means increasing borrowing costs across approximately $3.4B of WETH debt to address approximately $860M of rsETH and osETH loop exposure.

Merkl rebates can partially offset the additional borrowing costs, but do not eliminate the associated friction. Interest accrues continuously, while borrowers must manually claim rebates, stake them, and resupply before recovering their health factors. This creates an ongoing operational burden for borrowers, risks driving existing users to competing lending markets, and incurs additional fees for the DAO to run the Merkl campaigns.

Exchange Rate Growth Discounting Through CAPO

LST/LRT oracles on Aave combine three components:

  1. The ETH/USD price feed.
  2. The underlying protocol’s exchange rate.
  3. A CAPO adapter, which caps the exchange rate at a maximum value.

The CAPO adapter returns the lower of the live exchange rate and a maximum rate that grows at maxYearlyRatioGrowthPercent from a snapshot:

CAPO was designed to protect against upward manipulation of exchange rates. However, the same mechanism can also be used to limit the exchange rate appreciation recognized by Aave for specific collateral assets.

Setting maxYearlyRatioGrowthPercent to 0% effectively freezes the maximum permitted exchange rate at its initial snapshot. As the underlying asset continues to accrue staking yields any appreciation beyond this cap is no longer reflected in its collateral valuation on Aave. This does not change the underlying exchange rate or the asset’s actual redemption value; it only limits the value recognized by Aave’s oracle.

For leveraged positions, this creates a gradual deterioration in health factors: the collateral no longer benefits from exchange rate appreciation, while the WETH debt continues to accrue interest. Borrowers must progressively reduce leverage to maintain their health factors, making these loops increasingly unattractive and incentivizing an orderly unwind.

Each asset has its own CAPO adapter, allowing rsETH and osETH to be targeted independently without affecting other collateral assets or their respective ETH loops.

Projected Impact

The underlying exchange rates of rsETH and osETH currently grow at approximately 2.4% and 2.2% per year, respectively. Setting maxYearlyRatioGrowthPercent to 0% removes this appreciation from Aave’s collateral valuation. Meanwhile, WETH debt continues to accrue interest, progressively reducing the health factors of leveraged positions.

Assuming no borrower intervention and a constant WETH borrow rate, the time for a position to reach HF below 1 can be approximated as:

where (HF_0) is the initial health factor and (r) is the annualized WETH borrow rate.

Based on onchain positions as of 13 November 2026, the following table shows the cumulative collateral value of positions projected to reach HF below 1 under this scenario:

The projections show that CAPO adjustments alone can create meaningful deleveraging pressure, but the impact is relatively slow for rsETH. While osETH exposure is largely brought to liquidation within 18 months, the first material rsETH liquidations occur around month 6, with most of the exposure remaining beyond month 18.

This makes CAPO adjustments an effective mechanism for establishing a predictable exit timeline, but insufficient on their own to accelerate the rsETH unwind. The timeline can be shortened considerably by combining the CAPO adjustment with a series of carefully sized E-Mode liquidation threshold reductions, as discussed in the following section.

Accelerating the rsETH Unwind with E-Mode LT Reductions

rsETH loops sit in a dedicated E Mode category (“rsETH / ETH, wstETH, ETHx”), allowing their liquidation timeline to be shortened through targeted LT reductions without affecting other ETH loops on Core.

Rather than applying a single substantial LT reduction, the proposed approach uses a series of smaller adjustments, each calibrated against the health factors of remaining positions. This brings liquidation events forward incrementally while ensuring that no position becomes liquidatable immediately upon execution.

The process would follow a recurring cycle:

  1. Set the rsETH CAPO maxYearlyRatioGrowthPercent to 0%.
  2. Engagement window. Borrowers have time to unwind or migrate voluntarily.
  3. Assess the tightest remaining position. If it would reach HF < 1 within one month, make no change. Otherwise, reduce the E-Mode LT just enough to bring its projected liquidation to one month away.
  4. Wait for the liquidation and repeat Step 3 until no rsETH loops remain.

The first LT reduction is applied at the start of the cycle, once the engagement and migration window has closed. Its magnitude is determined by the health factors of the remaining positions at that point. Based on current positions, a reduction from 95% to 94.18% would bring the first projected liquidation forward from month 6 to month 1. However, as health factors continue to deteriorate under the 0% CAPO growth cap during the engagement window, the reduction required at the start of the cycle is expected to be smaller.

Following each liquidation episode, the next LT reduction is calibrated against the remaining positions using the same approach, bringing the next projected liquidation to one month ahead.

This approach ensures that each adjustment provides at least one month of notice before the next projected liquidation event. The interval can also be extended to accommodate available onchain liquidity and the beacon chain withdrawal queue.

Assuming passive borrowers, this iterative approach brings approximately 48% of rsETH collateral to liquidation within 12 months and approximately 72% within 24 months, compared with approximately 3% and 33%, respectively, under the CAPO adjustment alone.

Interaction with the ARFC’s migration path

The ARFC proposes adding wstETH, weETH and cbETH as collateral to the existing rsETH E Mode category, allowing borrowers to migrate their collateral without first repaying their WETH debt. We support this approach, as it provides borrowers with a straightforward migration path and facilitates the voluntary reduction of rsETH exposure.

However, subsequent E-Mode LT reductions would also affect positions that have already migrated to these assets, potentially penalizing borrowers who followed the proposed migration path. This needs to be addressed through appropriate sequencing of the migration and LT reduction processes.

This can be avoided by sequencing the migration and LT reduction processes:

  1. Migration window: Give rsETH borrowers time to swap their collateral into wstETH, weETH or cbETH within the rsETH E Mode category, as proposed in the ARFC.
  2. Move migrated positions to the standard ETH-correlated E Mode: Once migrated, borrowers can switch to the existing ETH-correlated E Mode, which has the same 93% / 95% LT / LTV parameters and WETH as a borrowable asset. This transition has no impact on their health factors.
  3. Begin the LT reduction cycle: Announce a fixed start date for the first LT reduction. By that point, the rsETH E-Mode category should contain only remaining rsETH positions, allowing subsequent LT reductions to target the intended exposure without affecting migrated borrowers.

This sequencing preserves the ARFC’s migration route while allowing the remaining rsETH loops to follow a shorter and more predictable unwinding timeline.

The DAO as Liquidator of Last Resort

In a worst case scenario with limited voluntary unwinding, the debt liquidated during these episodes may exceed available secondary market liquidity.

The DAO should therefore be prepared to fund these liquidations using treasury ETH and exit the seized rsETH through Kelp’s withdrawal queue.

Depending on the expected liquidation volume, the E-Mode liquidation bonus could also be increased ahead of each episode to compensate the DAO for the additional duration risk associated with holding seized rsETH until it can be redeemed through the withdrawal queue.

osETH Considerations

osETH shares the ETH correlated E-Mode with wstETH, weETH and cbETH. Therefore, E-Mode LT reductions cannot selectively target osETH positions without affecting other ETH loops. Setting maxYearlyRatioGrowthPercent to 0% on the osETH CAPO adapter remains the only targeted mechanism.

Overall Assessment

  • Targeted: CAPO adjustments affect only rsETH and osETH collateral valuations, leaving WETH borrowing costs and other ETH loops unchanged.
  • Predictable: The mechanism provides borrowers with time to unwind voluntarily, with liquidation timelines determined by individual position health factors.
  • Gradual: Borrowers can continue benefiting from the underlying exchange rate appreciation, but must progressively reduce leverage to maintain healthy positions.
  • Controlled market impact: Liquidations are distributed over time and occur partially, subject to the 50% close factor.
  • Accelerated rsETH unwind: E Mode LT reductions provide an additional mechanism to bring liquidation timelines forward without affecting other ETH loops, provided migrated positions are moved to the standard ETH correlated E Mode first.
  • Implementation: No new contracts or development are required. The analysis relies on updates to existing CAPO parameters and E Mode configuration.
  • Limitations: The rsETH CAPO adapter is currently shared across Aave V3 Core, V3 Prime and the V4 Kelp spoke. Should the CAPO adjustment be pursued, it could be scoped to the intended V3 markets by deploying a dedicated rsETH CAPO adapter and updating the corresponding oracle source, leaving other deployments that use the existing adapter unchanged. The treatment of other deployments is outside the scope of this analysis.

Conclusion and Potential Implementation Path

The following sequence combines the initial measures and migration path proposed in LlamaRisk’s ARFC with the targeted deleveraging mechanisms outlined in this analysis:

  1. Implement initial measures: Freeze osETH and set its LTV to 0%. rsETH is already frozen. Retain the ARFC’s proposed E-Mode additions to facilitate collateral migration.
  2. Apply CAPO adjustments: Set maxYearlyRatioGrowthPercent to 0% on the rsETH and osETH CAPO adapters.
  3. Engage and monitor: Work with issuers and the largest borrowers to facilitate voluntary migration and unwinding. Provide options to support borrowers, including tokenized positions in the beacon chain withdrawal queue and access to short term credit to bridge liquidity needs.
  4. Accelerate rsETH unwinding: Following the engagement and migration window, allow borrowers who have migrated to wstETH, weETH or cbETH to switch their positions to the standard “ETH correlated” E-Mode. Once migrated positions have exited the rsETH E-Mode, initiate the iterative LT reduction process for the remaining rsETH positions.
  5. Prepare for residual liquidations: Ensure the DAO is prepared to fund liquidations with treasury ETH where secondary market liquidity is insufficient, and exit seized rsETH and osETH through their respective withdrawal queues.

This analysis focuses solely on the CAPO parameter adjustments described in step 2. The subsequent measures, including the iterative E-Mode LT reductions for rsETH, will be reviewed separately and shared as needed.

governance_posts.description:
Summary

This ARFC proposes to update the collateral factors of the Coinbase tokenized equities on the Aave V4 Equities Hub on Base to the latest market data, under the current version of the collateral factor methodology. Most of the listed stocks have become more volatile since the start of 2026, and six of the eight reserves would move to a lower collateral factor. METAc and TSLAc would keep their current values. Maximum liquidation bonuses, liquidation fees, collateral risk, caps, and the USDC interest rate curve are unchanged.

Reserve Recent volatility, annualized Current Collateral Factor Proposed Collateral Factor
MSFTc 33.5% 79% 65%
AAPLc 25.0% 78% 65%
GOOGLc 38.3% 76% 65%
AMZNc 36.7% 73% 65%
NVDAc 43.4% 70% 65%
METAc 43.3% 65% 65%
TSLAc 49.2% 65% 65%
SPCXc 69.9% 55% 53%

Source: LlamaRisk and Aave, November 19, 2026

The new collateral factors would take effect as a new risk configuration on each of the six reserves. No position would be liquidated by the update.

Motivation

Stock volatility has risen since the start of 2026. The recent volatility of the typical S&P 500 stock, the geometric mean over the index members, has gone from 27.9% to 34.1% a year, and six of the seven stocks behind the Magnificent Seven (Mag7) tokens on the hub have followed, MSFT the most (19.4% to 33.5%) and AAPL the least (22.5% to 25.0%). TSLA, the most volatile of the seven, eased slightly, from 50.6% to 49.2%. Recent volatility weights each daily return more the more recent it is, with half the weight on the last 46 sessions.


Source: LlamaRisk, December 31, 2025 and November 19, 2026

The collateral factor of each reserve is derived from its stock’s recent volatility, and the proposed values are set on the latest data.

Collateral Factors

In Aave V4 the collateral factor is both the borrowing limit and the liquidation threshold. For a stock priced 24/5, it has to cover the largest fall from any off-hours price to the lowest price before five minutes past the next regular open, plus a 0.5% allowance for the feed’s deviation threshold. The haircut, the fall the collateral factor is built to absorb, is sized so that this fall exceeds it on one night per stock in ten years, with a 2020-type crash counted as one year in ten.

The haircut scales a forecast of the stock’s daily volatility over the next year by the size of a once-in-ten-years off-hours fall relative to daily volatility, measured across S&P 500 stocks. The forecast weights the stock’s recent moves and pulls them partly toward the market-wide level. The collateral factor is what remains after the haircut, the maximum liquidation bonus, and an allowance for interest while a position waits for liquidation, rounded down to a whole point and capped at 65%.

Reserve Recent volatility, annualized Haircut Max Liquidation Bonus Collateral Factor
MSFTc 33.5% 22.84% 5.50% 65%
AAPLc 25.0% 18.15% 5.50% 65%
GOOGLc 38.3% 25.42% 5.50% 65%
AMZNc 36.7% 24.56% 5.50% 65%
NVDAc 43.4% 28.09% 5.50% 65%
METAc 43.3% 28.05% 5.50% 65%
TSLAc 49.2% 30.99% 5.50% 65%
SPCXc 69.9% 42.51% 6.50% 53%

Source: LlamaRisk, November 19, 2026

The 65% maximum sets the collateral factor of MSFTc, AAPLc, GOOGLc, AMZNc, NVDAc, and METAc; at a 5.5% maximum liquidation bonus it corresponds to a minimum haircut of 31.25%. TSLAc’s haircut gives 65% directly. SPCXc is not an S&P 500 member, so its haircut uses the larger scale the method sets for stocks outside the index, and, with trading history since June 2026, its forecast leans more on the market-wide level. The interest allowance charges 24% a year over the longest market closure, 92 hours and 35 minutes, which is the top of the hub’s USDC rate curve; on SPCXc it includes the reserve’s 10% collateral risk.


Source: LlamaRisk and Aave, November 19, 2026

Implementation

The proposed collateral factors would be added as a new dynamic risk configuration on each of the six reserves, with their current maximum liquidation bonus and liquidation fee. In Aave V4 new positions open under the latest configuration, and an existing position moves to it when it borrows, withdraws, or changes the assets it uses as collateral; such an action goes through only if the position is healthy under the new collateral factors. No position would be liquidated by the update.

Specification

The update applies to the Mag-7 Spoke of the Equities Hub on Base. Collateral risk, caps, the dynamic liquidation bonus configuration, and the USDC interest rate curve are unchanged.

Base Equities Hub Mag-7 Spoke AAPLc 78.00% 65.00% 5.50% 10.00%
Base Equities Hub Mag-7 Spoke AMZNc 73.00% 65.00% 5.50% 10.00%
Base Equities Hub Mag-7 Spoke GOOGLc 76.00% 65.00% 5.50% 10.00%
Base Equities Hub Mag-7 Spoke MSFTc 79.00% 65.00% 5.50% 10.00%
Base Equities Hub Mag-7 Spoke NVDAc 70.00% 65.00% 5.50% 10.00%
Base Equities Hub Mag-7 Spoke SPCXc 55.00% 53.00% 6.50% 10.00%

Next Steps

  • Gather community feedback and service provider input on this ARFC during the forum discussion period, escalate it to an ARFC Snapshot, and, following a successful Snapshot, submit an AIP for an onchain vote to update the six reserves.

governance_posts.description:
Author: z0r0z (ross)
Date: 2026-11-23

Summary

This post introduces cBTC, a BTC token on Ethereum backed by locks held in self-custody on Bitcoin. We are asking whether the community and service providers would support onboarding its public ERC-20, tacBTC, to the Aave V3 Core Instance, the Aave V4 Core Hub, or both. We have no preference between the two and would follow the service providers.

Motivation

cBTC has been live on Ethereum mainnet since 2026-09-18. To mint it, the owner of the BTC creates a lock on Bitcoin, and a wstETH escrow of at least 1.5x the lock’s value is posted against it. The locker keeps the key. No custodian or committee holds the BTC.

The backing can be read on-chain. At block 26,478,414 the pool’s cbtcBackingSats() returns 22,252,699 sats, the reflection-attested total of live locks. The pool has no proxy, upgrade path, pause switch or admin key over escrow, exits or payouts.

Holders can keep cBTC as the public ERC-20 tacBTC or as a confidential note inside the pool. For Aave it would be a BTC collateral whose backing is verifiable on-chain and whose custody stays with the owner of the BTC.

Specification

Contracts: ConfidentialPool, CollateralEngine, tacBTC. Risk parameters and final configuration are for the Risk Service Providers to set.

How it works

  1. The BTC owner creates a lock on Bitcoin. The coins stay in an output the owner controls.
  2. Bitcoin’s state is proven on Ethereum with SP1 zk proofs of Bitcoin proof of work. Relayers are not trusted, and anyone can prove.
  3. cBTC is minted for the lock’s value, less a fee, once the escrow is posted. Anyone can fund the escrow.
  4. If a lock is spent without a redeem, the pool sees it and the escrow can be slashed into the insurance reserve by anyone. After a proven redeem, the escrow returns to its funder.

Supply is bounded by the reflected locks. The spec is SPEC section 5.7.

What you trust

  • Bitcoin and Ethereum consensus, SP1 and Groth16 soundness, and the sp1-helios sync committee.
  • Price feeds for escrow sizing: Chainlink BTC/USD and ETH/USD, and Lido’s wstETH rate, composed into a BTC-per-wstETH feed.
  • The ops multisig (2-of-5, one-hour delay) for the CollateralEngine, within on-chain bounds: escrow ratio between 1x and 10x, notice before borrower-adverse changes, and a minimum escrow grace window of 3 days. It can set oracle and CDP parameters, drive escrow enforcement and draw on the insurance reserve.

The lock is enforced economically, not by Bitcoin script: the locker holds the key and the escrow makes spending the lock unprofitable. If a script-enforced lock is proven for a tradable token, we would move to it. The pool lineage allows this through successor pools that users opt into.

Comparison with Babylon’s Trustless Bitcoin Vaults

Babylon’s column is taken from their docs.

cBTC Babylon TBV
What it is A token that moves and trades freely, public or inside a confidential pool A collateral record for one depositor’s vault
Lock enforcement Owner’s key plus a wstETH escrow of at least 1.5x at mint, slashable Bitcoin script with pre-signed spend paths and a zk proof verified through BABE, with a challenge period of about three days
Capital cost The wstETH escrow No depositor bond is described. The docs mention a claimer’s bond in the dispute process, with no amounts
Participants Anyone can prove, fund an escrow or slash Challengers are a static, permissioned registry. Direct-redemption liquidation is permissioned. The LLP liquidation path is permissionless
Transferable Yes The record is transfer-restricted to the Aave adapter: “There is no secondary market.”
Fungible Yes No. Each vault is one UTXO, segregated
Apps Anything that takes an ERC-20 Bound to one app at creation, with an adapter per app
Status Mainnet since 2026-09-18 Testnet per the docs as of Nov 23. Mainnet is targeted for Q4 2026, in phases

TBV gives a depositor a position in one app. cBTC is a token that can be held and used anywhere, and the escrow is the cost of that.

Where it is today

  • tacBTC public supply is 70,405 sats. Most cBTC is held in the pool as confidential notes.
  • 4,876 cUSD is borrowed against cBTC.
  • tacBTC has no deep on-chain pool. We would like input on how delegates and LPs want to bootstrap one.
  • Review history is in audit/AUDITS.md. The bug bounty is in SECURITY.md.

Disclaimer

We build Tacit and cBTC. This is our own asset, and we are not compensated by anyone for this post.

Next steps

  1. Gather community feedback in this thread. We will answer questions about the design.
  2. If a service provider is open to sponsoring it, Risk and Technical Service Providers post their assessments covering supply caps, rates and oracle for V3, V4 or both. We will provide what they need.
  3. If the response is positive, move to an ARFC, then Snapshot and an AIP.

governance_posts.description:
[ARFC] Sentora Externally Curated Hub & Spoke on Aave V4: Tempo OUSD Instance

Summary

This ARFC deploys a Sentora Hub and Spoke instance on Aave V4 on Tempo, under the framework established in the Sentora Externally Curated Hub & Spoke Framework ARFC. All governance, role, revenue and oversight terms of that framework apply unchanged.

  • One isolated Liquidity Hub on Tempo with OUSD as the sole borrowable asset, served by two Spokes: Sentora Tempo Bluechip and Sentora Tempo Yield.

  • Bluechip Spoke launch collateral is cbBTC and kBTC, with further BTC wrappers and XRP wrappers to be proposed through the framework’s optimistic listing process as they launch on Tempo. Yield Spoke launch collateral is PRIME, with USDe and PST pre-approved. Pre-approved assets carry zero caps and activate only once each is live on Tempo with a qualifying oracle.

  • Pre-approving the pending assets removes the need for a separate listing process per asset; cap activation follows the framework’s 48-hour timelock for risk-increasing actions.

  • The Aave DAO retains contract and admin ownership via the Governance Short Executor, receives 50% of instance revenue, and authorises no credit lines to or from DAO Hubs.

  • OUSD supply is net new to Aave, supported by incentive programs coordinated with the Tempo ecosystem.

Motivation

Tempo is a payments-focused network where OUSD is a primary settlement stablecoin, and its integrators are seeking onchain yield for idle OUSD balances. An Aave V4 Hub gives those balances a curated lending venue on the same network, without bridging to Ethereum. PRIME is the Yield Spoke’s launch collateral because it trades directly against OUSD on Tempo, with approximately $20M of committed market-maker liquidity, which gives liquidators a single-hop exit. Establishing the Hub now also provides the base layer for protected (insured) vault products on Tempo once collateral yields support them. Splitting collateral into a Bluechip Spoke and a Yield Spoke caps each risk class’s draw on Hub liquidity independently and keeps BTC wrapper positions, and later XRP wrapper positions, separate from yield-bearing collateral.

Market Structure

  • Hub: one Sentora Liquidity Hub on Tempo, isolated from all other Aave markets and from the other Sentora Hubs.

  • Borrowable liquidity: OUSD only. All other assets are collateral-only, with 0% interest and a zero draw cap.

  • Spokes: Sentora Tempo Bluechip, OUSD debt against cbBTC and kBTC at launch, with further BTC wrappers and XRP wrappers to follow as they launch on Tempo; Sentora Tempo Yield, OUSD debt against PRIME at launch, with USDe and PST pre-approved.

Instance Management

Identical to the Ethereum instance. Sentora is operational manager through revocable roles and owns no deployed contracts:

  • grantRole(SENTORA_RESTRICTIVE_ROLE, sentoraAddress, 0), risk-reducing

  • grantRole(SENTORA_MANAGED_ROLE, sentoraAddress, 172800), risk-increasing (48 hours)

  • grantRole(SENTORA_MANAGED_ROLE, sentoraRiskSteward, 0), risk-reducing

Emergency actions (pause, freeze, halt, cap resets) execute through the Restrictive Role with no delay. Risk-reducing parameter changes execute through the Risk Steward with no delay. Risk-increasing and ambiguous changes, including IRM and liquidation configuration changes and activation of caps on pre-approved assets, are scheduled on the AccessManager and wait 48 hours. During that window the Aave DAO executor can cancel any individual scheduled operation, and the DAO can revoke Sentora’s role grants by governance proposal.

Collateral not listed in this ARFC, and any further Hub, follows the framework’s 2-week optimistic review. An objection from an appointed service provider moves the item to a binding Snapshot, and Sentora cannot schedule or deploy while it is pending.

Aave DAO Oversight

The Aave DAO executor holds admin roles over the Tempo Hub, both Spokes, their configurators and the AccessManager. Upgrades and role assignment are not delegated. Ownership does not make the DAO or its service providers responsible for risk management on this instance.

Sentora will publish a monthly report covering supply, borrow, utilization, cap usage, queued operations, role changes and revenue for all instances.

Aave DAO Alignment

  • OUSD is the only borrowable asset. USDC and USDT are excluded.

  • The Liquidity Fee is set to 20% on every asset in the AIP payload. Sentora may raise it and will not lower it; a reduction below 20% is outside Sentora’s mandate and grounds for role revocation.

  • All protocol revenue (reserve factor, liquidation fees and related streams) is split 50% Aave DAO and 50% Sentora, settled onchain.

Specification

Assets in gray are approved for listing with zero add caps. Each activates only once the asset is live on Tempo with a qualifying oracle, through a 48-hour timelocked cap increase.

Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, on-chain liquidity, and position health observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

Aave V3 Core:

USDC Interest Rate Model (Aave V3 Core)
